title: Booleans and comparisons

curriculum.title: Booleans and Comparisons Without Branches
curriculum.answer:
### Booleans from comparisons
A comparison asks a question about two numbers and answers with a Boolean value: `True` or `False`. Python prints those two words with a capital first letter. No decision statement is needed to see them; `print` can show the answer directly.

The main symbols are less than, greater than, equality, and inequality:

- `x < y` asks whether `x` is smaller.
- `x > y` asks whether `x` is larger.
- `x == y` asks whether the values are the same.
- `x != y` asks whether the values are different.
- `x <= y` and `x >= y` include the equal case.

Every variable below is assigned before it is used, so each example can run on its own.

```python
x = 3
y = 5
print(x < y)
print(x == y)
```
```text
True
False
```

The first print statement displays `True` because 3 is smaller than 5. The second print statement displays `False` because 3 and 5 are not the same value. Each comparison produces one Boolean, and `print` displays it.

Comparisons can also be stored in a named result for later use:

```python
a = 10
b = 6
is_greater = a > b
is_equal = a == b
print(is_greater)
print(is_equal)
```
```text
True
False
```

Here `is_greater` becomes `True` because 10 is larger than 6, while `is_equal` becomes `False`. The variable keeps the Boolean answer.

Two common mistakes are reversing order and mixing up assignment with comparison. `m > n` and `m < n` ask opposite questions, so only one can be `True` when the numbers differ. A single `=` binds a name to a value, while a double `==` compares left and right and returns `True` or `False`. Check the direction of `<` and `>` and count the equal signs carefully.

exercise.title: Less-than check
exercise.instructions: You are given two numbers x and y. Assign to is_less whether x is less than y. For example, if x is 2 and y is 7, is_less should become True. Do not assign new values to x or y; only assign the comparison result to is_less.

fresh_exercise.title: Equality check
fresh_exercise.instructions: You are given two numbers m and n. Assign to is_equal whether m and n hold the same numeric value. For example, if m is 4 and n is 4, is_equal should become True, and if they differ it should become False. Do not assign new values to m or n.
